description: Explicit public snapshot strategies for paths blocked by audit_public_release. First matching rule wins.

strategy_rules.reason: Migration manifests are required public metadata; sanitize string values with JSON parse-transform-dump while preserving their structure.
Only authorized owners may select the repository code license. The default snapshot carries a blocking notice instead of invented license terms.
Do not redistribute the approximately 19 MB detailed exposure artifact; emit only a hash commitment and public disposition summary.
Retain reviewed acquisition plans while replacing machine-local transport defaults in the export copy.
Blocked rehearsal records are live access, route, run, or governance evidence and are excluded; release-ready public plans remain included through the audit manifest.
Blocked historical review and execution material is internal and is not needed for the public engineering surface.
The blocked access dossier contains internal route evidence and is excluded pending a separate public rewrite.
Internal gateway/run governance design is excluded from the public snapshot.
Canary authority identifiers are internal governance material; public commitments are released separately.
Keep core design documentation, sanitizing only detected machine-local infrastructure or private run identifiers in the export copy.
Keep current engineering documentation with machine-local route examples sanitized in the export copy.
Migration documentation is public-core material; replace workstation-specific examples only in the staged copy.
Preserve research implementation while sanitizing only detected infrastructure literals in the export copy.
Preserve public automation while sanitizing only detected infrastructure literals in the export copy.
Preserve engineering tools while sanitizing only detected infrastructure literals and private run IDs in the export copy.
Preserve model-free and unit test coverage, applying the same export-only literal sanitization as production helpers.
Preserve tooling tests, applying the same export-only literal sanitization as the tools under test.
